verses.text: Now in those days, when the number of the disciples was multiplying, a complaint arose from the Hellenists  against the Hebrews, because their widows were neglected in the daily service.
The twelve summoned the multitude of the disciples and said, “It is not appropriate for us to forsake the word of God and serve tables.
Therefore select from among you, brothers, seven men of good report, full of the Holy Spirit and of wisdom, whom we may appoint over this business.
But we will continue steadfastly in prayer and in the ministry of the word.”
These words pleased the whole multitude. They chose Stephen, a man full of faith and of the Holy Spirit, Philip, Prochorus, Nicanor, Timon, Parmenas, and Nicolaus, a proselyte of Antioch;
whom they set before the apostles. When they had prayed, they laid their hands on them.
The word of God increased and the number of the disciples multiplied in Jerusalem exceedingly. A great company of the priests were obedient to the faith.
Stephen, full of faith and power, performed great wonders and signs among the people.
But some of those who were of the synagogue called “The Libertines”, and of the Cyrenians, of the Alexandrians, and of those of Cilicia and Asia arose, disputing with Stephen.
They weren’t able to withstand the wisdom and the Spirit by which he spoke.
Then they secretly induced men to say, “We have heard him speak blasphemous words against Moses and God.”
They stirred up the people, the elders, and the scribes, and came against him and seized him, and brought him in to the council,
and set up false witnesses who said, “This man never stops speaking blasphemous words against this holy place and the law.
For we have heard him say that this Jesus of Nazareth will destroy this place, and will change the customs which Moses delivered to us.”
All who sat in the council, fastening their eyes on him, saw his face like it was the face of an angel.

footnotes.content: Even as the church grew, complaint crept in—widows neglected in the daily distribution. I've learned that rapid blessing can hide slow neglect if we're not watching. The apostles didn't dismiss the concern; they stopped and listened.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The twelve were clear: we can't abandon God's word to manage tables. It's not that tables don't matter—it's that some callings require your whole heart. Wisdom often looks like honest boundary-keeping in the service of the Gospel.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Seven men of good report, full of the Holy Spirit and wisdom. They didn't hire for efficiency or connections—they looked for the Spirit's presence. Holiness and wisdom working together mark the faithful servant.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The apostles committed themselves to prayer and the ministry of the word. I see now that their faithfulness to their calling—not busyness—built the early church. They knew what they'd been given to do and wouldn't be drawn from it.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Stephen stands out even in the list—full of faith and of the Holy Spirit. Notice that. He wasn't just competent; he carried the presence of God visibly. Sometimes one name in a passage carries the whole weight of what's to come.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: They set the seven before the apostles, and then prayed and laid hands on them. Laying on of hands was no ceremony here—it was the apostolic blessing, the authority and covering of the church's elders passed to those set apart for this work.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The word of God increased, and the disciples multiplied. Even a great company of priests came to faith—those who'd guarded the temple now followed the Lord. When the Spirit moves, not even the most settled hearts resist for long.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Stephen, full of faith and power, performed great wonders and signs. This wasn't something he had to earn; the Spirit did the work through him because his heart was settled in Christ. The faithful servant becomes a vessel for the miraculous.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: From the Libertines' synagogue—freed slaves or their descendants—from Cyrene, Alexandria, Cilicia, and Asia they rose to dispute with Stephen. These diaspora communities, far from home, carried their convictions fiercely. The conflict wasn't local piety; it spanned the empire's trading routes.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: They couldn't withstand the wisdom and the Spirit by which he spoke. Stephen's words carried weight not because of his rhetoric, but because the Holy Spirit itself stood behind them. We learn: the power lies not in us, but in the One we yield to.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: They secretly induced men to say Stephen had blasphemed Moses and God. When truth can't be overcome, it's covered with lies. This is how the world has always answered the faithful: not with better argument, but with slander.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: They stirred up the people, elders, and scribes—a machinery of fear and duty. They seized Stephen and brought him to the council. Watch how quickly accusation becomes motion, how quickly motion becomes violence, when hearts are closed.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: False witnesses said Stephen never stopped speaking against the holy place and the law. The irony cuts deep: they used falsehood to defend what they believed was holy. The heart that hardens in self-defense learns to swallow its own lies.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: They claimed Stephen said Jesus would destroy the place and change Moses' customs. What were they so afraid of? Perhaps they sensed that the temple and the law were no longer the center—that Christ Himself was breaking open what they'd built to guard Him.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: All in the council fastened their eyes on him and saw his face like the face of an angel. Readers today hear an echo of this in our own trials: when we stand for Christ, His peace and presence can show through us in ways beyond our own strength. Even in threat, there's a light.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
